newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MPs approve mandate for Iraq air patrols.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MPs approve mandate for Iraq air patrols.

text.p: Turkish MPs on Thursday approved a six-month extension of a U.S.-led aerial surveillance operation to protect the Kurdish regions of northern Iraq.
The speaker of parliament said deputies passed a motion to extend the mandate for a joint U.S.-British air force based at the Incirlik air base in southern Turkey.

The force has been patrolling the skies of northern Iraq to protect Kurds from any attack by Baghdad since the Gulf War ended in 1991. The mandate was last renewed in December 1996 and expires on June 30.
The operation, previously named Provide Comfort, was redubbed Northern Watch following the withdrawal of French aircraft at the end of last year.
Turkish deputies have often complained the air shield helped to create a power vacuum exploited by Kurdish rebels using bases in northern Iraq.
Turkish security forces, involved for six weeks in an anti-rebel operation in northern Iraq, have now mostly withdrawn from the region.
